title: Token Impact Timeline (Bento) — Cost Attribution & Pricing Patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a compact, timeline-first lens (called 'Bento') that surfaces per-session and per-token cost impact across time. The view combines an interactive timeline, row-level attribution cards, and exportable pricing slices so product and finance users can understand who/what drove cost spikes and test pricing scenarios. This ticket covers visual language, interaction patterns for rollups and drilldowns, CSV/JSON export patterns, and a small responsive prototype for the Console dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Bento timeline mock with compressed timeline + session lanes available in Figma
Row-level token cost cards that show breakdown: base model cost, quantization discount, batching savings, cache hit delta
Attribution flow that traces a token cost back to prompting pattern and selected model variant
Export formats: small CSV with per-token rows, JSON export with session grouping, and a pre-built 'pricing scenario' JSON for offline simulation
Role-aware UI: owners see cost breakdown; viewers see anonymized counts; billing admins can download raw exports
Prototype responds to common Console states: canary rollout switch, fallback to cheaper variant, and dedicated capacity throttling
Design handoff artifacts (specs + tokens) uploaded to Drive and Confluence with component library tokens
design_notes: Primary goal: make the 'why' behind cost spikes obvious in under 6s — reduce detective work for PMs and Finance
Use a compact card grid (Bento) under the timeline for quick comparisons; cards surface 3 signals: cost delta, traffic source, and scoring impact
Provide progressive disclosure: aggregate view -> session lanes -> per-message -> per-token breakdown
Color system aligns with Console semantics: positive = cost reduction (green), negative = cost increase (amber/red); neutral = muted gray
Include micro-interactions for export: 'snap-to-range' and 'include prompt text' toggles (default off for PII concerns)
Pagination/export caps: default download limited to 50k tokens; billing admins can request full export via API
tradeoffs: Showing full per-token text inline aids debugging but raises PII/PII-removal complexity — default to token ids + hashed prompt snippets
High-fidelity timeline with continuous zoom is expensive in the client; we opt for discrete zoom levels (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d) with server-side aggregation
Including batching and cache metrics increases clarity but requires cross-team infra signals (runtime and billing) which may lag — show 'last synced' timestamp and graceful stale state
Export size vs usability: CSV is simple but large; JSON includes grouping and pricing scenario metadata for reproducibility
